$comment: Defects a person or an independent review found, labelled with the gate that should catch each one. `pages` are rendered page numbers of the specimen's stored build (null for a deck-level defect). `expectedGate` is a code from the page gates, plan gates, variety or craft gates, `BUILD:<measure>` for a build bar, or RENDERED_OVERLAP for the Chromium overlap audit; null means no gate measures it yet, which is a gap rather than a mistake in the label. gate-validity.mjs replays the stored specimens through the gates and reports per-gate precision and recall against this table.

defects.defect: The answer's conditions are stated four different ways across the answer, the summary, the scorecard and the takeaway.
Two different load factors are both called 'load factor', so the same measure reads 64.9% on two pages and 78.4% on two others.
A rival's fleet and order book differ on every page that states them.
About a dozen titles are counts or rankings with no implication, so the title spine stalls from section 02 onwards.
The deck shipped two empty picture frames on a picture-pair page, and passed everything.
The run wrote its four-point readiness scale as plain words rather than harvey balls, deliberately.
Five findings split into two columns of three and two, each column starting at a different height.
A list under a kpi floated away from it, leaving a void between the number and the first thing said about it.
The twelve-market readiness column stayed plain text even after the anchor-word fix.
In a dense table the harvey disc overlapped the word beside it.
On a twelve-row scorecard the single implication chevron sat on the France row and read as a verdict on France.
'$46m, 11-month filing' arrived in a box two and a half times the size of its own sentence, with the leader dropping out of the empty half.

A table split over two pages draws its in-cell bars at two different scales - 0 to 1500 on the first half, 0 to 450 on the second - so a $440m bar is drawn longer than a $1,148m bar one page earlier. Repeated on the appendix pair.

A five-step staircase inside a plot frame with an axis, whose blocks are all 75px tall while the values printed on them are 126, 143, 136, 148 and 330 minutes. The 330-minute payoff is drawn the same size as the 126-minute opener.
The answer page and the closing takeaway state the screen answer as Marvel unconditionally; three later pages recommend DC on screen for the one-evening reader.

Three axis categories printed on top of one another ('Superman (2025)ther DC featuAlsDC features'); a period bracket rule struck through a legend; two-line category labels colliding into one seven-line block.
Both halves of an appendix table carry a Total row that sums the 'Multiple (x budget)' column: 41.4 and 30.9. A sum of budget multiples is not a quantity.
Half a page is an empty gradient rectangle, with body text beside it explaining that the frame holds a specimen image because the characters are trademarked.
Commentary blocks headed 'Six of the twelve are DC' beside a chart whose labels are tagged '(DC)'; bar sub-labels repeating the bar labels word for word.
